 Medium

 Print Anthony Davis. Image via: Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images The Golden State Warriors are among the most realistic suitors for an Anthony Davis trade, based on a Nov. 11 ranking of the top trade targets in the NBA. The ranking places Davis sixth and lists Golden State first among his possible landing spots, with Phoenix and Toronto also named. He is averaging 25.7 points and 9.7 rebounds in nine games with the Washington Wizards. Golden State has won each of its last five games, most recently a 138-87 rout of New Orleans on Nov. 9. Any deal would need salary matching. A separate report says Draymond Green or Jimmy Butler would likely go to Washington to make the money work. Neither team has confirmed talks, and no agreement has been reported. Field Details 
 Category NBA trade rumor 
 Player Anthony Davis 
 Current Team Washington Wizards 
 Rumored Team Golden State Warriors (Phoenix Suns and Toronto Raptors also named) 
 Contract Status 3-year, $175,369,698 
 Salary Cap Hit $54,126,450 listed for 2026 
 Trade Likelihood Rumor stage; ranked second most likely of three Warriors targets, behind Norman Powell and ahead of Franz Wagner 
 Latest Insider Update Nov. 11 ranking lists Davis sixth among trade targets and Golden State first among landing spots; Green or Butler floated as the salary piece 
 Why the Warriors want an Anthony Davis trade
 Anthony Davis. Image via: Stacy Revere/Getty Images Golden State has been linked to Davis since last offseason. Interest has resurfaced as the Warriors put together a strong early record behind Stephen Curry. One report calls rookie Yaxel Lendeborg the team’s second-best player and treats him and Curry as the only untouchable names. Brandin Podziemski and Moses Moody are viewed as more movable for the right price. The report adds Mike Dunleavy could stand pat while the roster builds chemistry. Davis is 33, stands 6-foot-10 and weighs 253 pounds. One report says he fits Curry’s timeline, with both contracts ending around the same time. Green is 36 and is averaging 2.8 points, 4.9 rebounds and 7.6 assists through nine games. His listed 2026 earnings are $25,892,857, compared with $54,126,450 for Davis. Using those figures, Green alone would leave a gap of about $28.2 million, so the package would need more salary. Join conversation

 What reports say about a possible Anthony Davis trade
 A Nov. 11 ranking of league-wide trade targets puts Davis sixth and names Golden State, Phoenix and Toronto as possible landing spots. The report points to his injury history, his reported desire for a new contract and his frustration in Washington as reasons his stay may not last. It also says talk of a return to the Los Angeles Lakers has no support. A separate report ranks Davis second most likely among three players linked to Golden State, behind Chicago’s Norman Powell and ahead of Orlando’s Franz Wagner, and expects competition for all three. On Monday, Davis scored 44 points with 13 rebounds on 16-of-21 shooting in a 122-111 loss at Detroit. Anthony Davis trade value by the numbers: stats

 Davis has 10 All-Star selections, five All-NBA nods and five All-Defensive team picks. He won the 2020 NBA title with the Lakers, led the league in blocks three times and earned the 2016-17 All-Star Game MVP award. New Orleans drafted him first overall in 2012 out of Kentucky, and he was named to the NBA 75th Anniversary Team. Davis is shooting 53.3 percent from the field and 37.5 percent from three through nine games. Reports tie his contract to Curry’s timeline and say he wants a new deal.
